name: Harhas
overview: Harhas is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Tikvah, as recorded in 2 Kings 22:14. There is no information about his tribe or additional personal details. His mention is brief and specific, highlighting his familial connection rather than his own actions or status.
namesAndTitles: The name Harhas appears as a proper name in Scripture without an indicated meaning or divine origin. An alternate form of his name, Hasrah, is also recorded in 2 Chronicles 34:22, but similarly lacks a given meaning or title significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Harhas as the father of Tikvah, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Harhas's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his daughter Tikvah, who is mentioned in the context of King Josiah's reforms. While Harhas himself does not play a direct role, his identification as Tikvah's father provides genealogical context within the historical setting of 2 Kings. This connection situates him within the broader narrative of Judah's religious restoration.
